defects.title: Caller-controlled process allowlist could launder execution authority
defects.failure: Runtime v0.1 accepted the process allowlist at invocation time instead of binding it to a runtime-minted capability.
defects.repair: Process policy is sealed at mint time; current runtime additionally requires canonical absolute executable identity plus fingerprint and executes the opened pinned file descriptor.

defects.title: Arbitrary Python callable could cross async capability boundary
defects.failure: Runtime v0.1 async.map accepted a caller-supplied callable, allowing host behavior outside the capability policy.
defects.repair: async.map now accepts only runtime-owned named operations permitted by the sealed async.compute capability policy; callable laundering is an explicit negative test.

defects.title: Parser/canonical hashes could erase operator literal identity
defects.failure: Default Lark trees can omit anonymous literal terminals, allowing meaning-changing operator mutations such as > versus < to collapse in structural fingerprints.
defects.repair: Literal-preserving validation/canonicalization was added and the production frontend advanced to V7 named operator nodes with semantic mutation discriminators.

defects.title: Strict frontend CI was wired to superseded V4 grammar
defects.failure: The active CI path still selected V4 after full-corpus evidence had moved to later repairs, guaranteeing stale failure/evidence.
defects.repair: Strict/full-corpus validation was rewired through the current repaired grammar path and target gate now explicitly selects V7.

defects.title: Two executable compiler slices briefly disagreed on Int division semantics
defects.failure: A new vertical-slice implementation treated Int/Int division as Real while the integrated BASE compiler preserved Int arithmetic semantics.
defects.repair: The extra pure toolchain was converted into a compatibility facade over tools/claycode_base_compiler.py, leaving one executable arithmetic/type/evaluator/lowering semantics.

defects.title: Andreas target gate referenced obsolete insecure application proxy API
defects.failure: The target preflight still called the old app suite after runtime authority hardening, so it could neither execute current runtime semantics nor serve as a valid preflight.
defects.repair: Target gate now runs the sealed-capability application proxy v2 plus current package and real effect-runtime bridge gates.

defects.title: Package linker currently requires globally unique bare function symbols
defects.impact: Packages and deterministic import resolution work, but module-qualified symbol namespaces remain a language/toolchain extension rather than current BASE behavior.
defects.acceptance_effect: Does not block the current BASE package gate as long as duplicate symbols fail closed and acceptance fixtures remain within the frozen subset.
defects.next_test: Add an explicit two-module same-name fixture before introducing namespace-qualified calls.

note: Missing target-host execution or missing acceptance receipts are tracked as release evidence gaps, not silently reclassified as software defects. WP14 still fails until those evidence gaps are closed.
